audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted their own why text: Level 2 read Ornn while whys[1] says to play for CS and dodge the stun; Levels 4-5 and Level 6 read Skill while whys[3]/[4] describe Ornn winning both; 2+ items read Ornn while whys[6] says Tahm out-sustains and out-grinds in even gold.
audit.why: Ornn's advantage is the 3-to-6 window before Thick Skin and health scaling refund his chip. The packet chart agrees on all four rows.
audit.corrected: Level 2 -> Skill, Levels 4-5 -> Ornn, Level 6 -> Ornn, 2+ items -> Skill, matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 said only that 'Tahm Kench's ultimate changes the math', and the content layer describes Ornn's own R as a 'double knock-up' delivered on cast.
audit.why: The Tahm Kench-side mirror audit already established this and I am restating it: Call of the Forge God's first pass deals damage, slows and applies Brittle — the knock-up is on the recast charge into the elemental. Presenting it as an unconditional double knock-up teaches the player to commit on a cast that does not lock anyone down.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and whys[4] rewritten to put the knock-up on the recast.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stack system — the thing that actually governs this lane — was never explained. Tongue Lash was treated as a stun on demand ('Get Q-stunned', 'Respect his Q tongue stun'), and the page never said that three stacks of An Acquired Taste are also what makes Devour castable on you.
audit.why: Riot text, Q: 'Applies a stack of An Acquired Taste to enemy champions. If the champion already has 3 stacks, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed.' Riot text, P: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion.' So sitting at two stacks is the danger state, and disengaging to let stacks fall off is a real, actionable play the page never offered.
audit.corrected: Stack rule stated in tldr, dontsFull[0].d, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was generic; the mechanism it answers was misattributed throughout the content layer to a 'grey-health passive'.
audit.why: Grey health and the shield conversion are Thick Skin (E) on a 3s cooldown, not the passive — the passive is An Acquired Taste. Tongue Lash also heals him on champion hit. Both are flagged in the missing-interactions file, and both mean Ornn's poke partially refunds itself unless Grievous Wounds exists.
audit.corrected: report[8] now names Thick Skin and states what it refunds; breakdown.cooldowns gives its 3s cooldown.

edits.before: Dodge his tongue — W-brittle, E-knock him up. Ornn wins the Abyssal Dive cooldown windows.
edits.after: Tongue Lash only stuns at three Acquired Taste stacks — break the stacks before it does.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Tahm Kench's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God only knocks up on the recast charge — the first pass is damage, slow and Brittle. Land both and his 21s Abyssal Dive cannot answer.

edits.before: His escape + shield. Trade when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 — his engage and his escape. Fight once it is spent.

edits.before: That is Tahm Kench's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Three stacks means Tongue Lash stuns and Devour is live — never sit on two.

edits.before: Track Tahm Kench's Abyssal Dive: His escape + shield. Trade when down. When it is down — W-E + R him.
edits.after: An Acquired Taste is the real clock: at three stacks his Q stuns and his R can swallow you whole.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His escape + shield. Trade when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench Tongue Lash: 7s at rank 1, 900 range — it stuns only at three Acquired Taste stacks. - Abyssal Dive: 21s at rank 1, his engage and his escape. - Thick Skin: 3s — he banks your chip and returns it as shield.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (forge-upgradeable), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Plated Steelcaps. Add anti-heal (Thornmail component early) — his healing fights your grind.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (forge-upgradeable), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Plated Steelcaps. Thick Skin refunds your chip as shield and grey health — buy Grievous Wounds early.

edits.before: R's double knock-up plus E-Q chains CC longer than his W devour can cleanse, winning the all-in.
edits.after: R's first pass slows and Brittles; the recast knock-up plus E-Q is what wins the all-in.

notes: A systematic slot error runs through this matchup's content layer: it calls Abyssal Dive (W) a 'devour' and a 'self-eat cleanse' in whys[3], whys[6], spikes[1], spikes[3], mid, late, wants.you[1], wants.you[2] and wants.foe[0]. W is a leap that knocks up; Devour is the R; and nothing in Tahm's kit cleanses CC by eating himself. It also calls grey health a 'passive' when it is Thick Skin (E). I fixed the full layer and one content string; the rest needs a single sweep rather than nine separate band-limited rewrites. Per the mirror, Ornn's R knock-up is on the recast only — the phrase 'R double knock-up' appears on many other Ornn matchup pages and is likely wrong there too. UNVERIFIED and untouched: the 'unstoppable' claim on Bellows Breath in whys[2]/early.
